transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Tom Reyes (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Head of Search, SoundWave); Diego Alvarez (Staff ML Engineer, SoundWave); Sofia Tran (CTO, SoundWave)
Shared artifacts: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/soundwave-demo | Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/soundwave-poc

Auto-summary: Short demo of Hosted API embeddings + rerank. Walkthrough of typical search flow (embed -> candidate retrieve -> rerank) and Redwood Console/Optimize tips for batching and caching. Discussed security (SOC2, KMS, SSO) and next steps for 2-week POC.

Topics: embeddings latency, rerank scoring, batching, KV cache, cost tradeoffs, data retention/KMS, pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. We're Maya (Redwood) and Tom is our solutions engineer, we'll run through a short hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking and then cover pilot options.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we run a transcript search product for podcasts, roughly 200M docs, but our search index is mostly recent episodes. We're trying to get better relevance on longtail queries.
[00:34] Tom Reyes: Cool, thanks Priya. We'll show the simple flow: query -> embeddings -> candidate retrieve -> rerank. We'll demo the API calls and then show how Optimize recommends batching/quant settings for cost.
[00:50] Diego Alvarez: One ask up front — can you keep data out of logs? We need to ensure audio transcripts don't persist in plaintext in your logs.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we have a mode where logs are disabled for customer requests and you can bring your own KMS for encryption at rest. We'll include the SOC2 and KMS docs in the pack.
[01:20] Sofia Tran: Also curious about latency numbers for embeddings at the scale — we can't add 300ms per search.
[01:30] Tom Reyes: Totally. For hosted API we've seen typical embedding latencies in the 70-150ms range depending on model and batch size; rerank calls (single query against top-k candidates) tend to be 20-80ms per candidate pair on our hosted fleet. If you want sub-100ms end-to-end we often suggest a small dedicated pool or caching hot prefixes.
[01:54] Priya Nair: Is that for a single vector call? What about batching many queries?
[01:58] Tom Reyes: Batching helps linearly — you can send up to N per request; our SDK does automatic batching, and Redwood Optimize will recommend batch sizes based on your sequence length distribution. But note there is a latency vs cost tradeoff: larger batches reduce cost per vector but increase tail latency.
[02:18] Diego Alvarez: When you say rerank, are you returning a score or the re-written text?
[02:22] Tom Reyes: The hosted rerank endpoint returns a relevance score for each doc vs the query and optional structured outputs if you want (like reason tokens). Typically we do embed + retrieve (FAISS or Pinecone) then call rerank for top 50. We also support an embeddings-only rerank where you compute dot-product client-side, but our rerank model usually improves quality.
[02:45] Priya Nair: How does this tie into your Console/Optimize?
[02:48] Maya Chen: In the Console you'll see per-route token/embedding cost, latency histograms, and Optimize will surface suggestions — like quantization suggestions, recommended batch sizes, and cache TTLs for your workload.
[03:05] Sofia Tran: Any examples of cost savings with Optimize?
[03:09] Tom Reyes: We had a customer that cut embedding costs 30% by switching to a quantized model and enabling prefix caching. The Optimize tool recommended a different kernel and reduced unnecessary reranks by caching top intents.
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: Sounds promising. For the POC we want to run 1k queries and compare precision@10 between our current system and Redwood's reranked results — we can supply the sample.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Perfect. That aligns with our typical pilot — we run the sample, share the benchmark spreadsheet with expected columns (query, gold docs, candidate list, scores) and we do a side-by-side.
[03:48] Priya Nair: Can you walk the team through an actual API call?
[03:52] Tom Reyes: Sure — I'll share my screen.
[04:00] [screen share noise] Tom Reyes: Ok, so here is a cURL example for embeddings:
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Body: { "model": "rw-embed-large", "input": ["your query text"] }
Response: { "data": [{ "embedding": [0.01, -0.3, ...], "index": 0 }] }

[04:28] Tom Reyes: For rerank we provide an endpoint like POST /v1/rerank with payload { "model": "rw-rerank-v1", "query": "...", "candidates": [{"id":"doc1","text":"..."}, ...] } and response includes scores array and an optional explain field.
[04:50] Priya Nair: Are candidates limited in size? We have very long transcripts.
[04:55] Tom Reyes: For long docs we recommend chunking, and Optimize can suggest chunk sizes. Also, we do KV cache for prefixes — note sometimes it's transcribed as "KV cash" in older logs, so apologies if you saw that.
[05:10] Diego Alvarez: If we chunk, what about semantic coherence for rerank? We often lose context between chunks.
[05:16] Tom Reyes: Great point — we rerank on the top candidate chunks and can optionally aggregate scores per document. We also support a document-level embed if you precompute document-level vectors (you can do coarse+fine retrieval).
[05:30] Sofia Tran: On security, can you confirm SSO support and RBAC?
[05:34] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, SAML tested with several vendors. RBAC is available in the Console so you can lock down routes and keys. We'll include screenshots in the security pack.
[05:48] Priya Nair: Any mention of data residency? We need EU-only storage for EU customers.
[05:53] Maya Chen: We have region controls in Hosted; we can pin your tenant to eu-west-1 region and optionally use Private for strict on-prem. We'll send details.
[06:05] Diego Alvarez: How does billing look for a POC? We don't want surprises.
[06:09] Maya Chen: For pilots we typically provide a usage estimate and a short-term trial bucket; we'll include a pricing sheet. POC billing can be usage-based but we can set caps and alerts.
[06:20] Priya Nair: Nice. On quality, do you have any guidance on evaluation metrics? We use MAP/precision@k and NDCG.
[06:27] Tom Reyes: Those are great. For rerank we usually report precision@10, NDCG@10, and latency percentiles. We'll populate the benchmark sheet with those columns.
[06:38] [09:20] Tom Reyes: (demo continues — showing Console) Here you can see per-route token breakdown, and Optimize highlights that your sequence lengths are heavy-tailed — Optimize recommends two quant profiles: q4_0 for embeddings and q4_k for the rerank model to maximize throughput without degrading quality.
[07:00] Priya Nair: Is quantization supported on hosted? Any quality regressions?
[07:04] Tom Reyes: We validate quant profiles on your prompt set; small regressions are possible but Optimize runs can recommend the safe profile. We'll share model calibration notes.
[07:18] Diego Alvarez: For throughput, do you support autoscaling dedicated pools? We're concerned about burst episodes when a show drops.
[07:25] Maya Chen: Yep — Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity. For Hosted we have fallback routing and burst buffers but Dedicated gives you SLA-backed throughput.
[07:40] Priya Nair: How hard is integration? Our stack is Node + Python microservices.
[07:44] Tom Reyes: Very straightforward — our SDKs are in Python, Node, and Go. Example integration is two endpoints: embed (bulk) and rerank. We can share a minimal repo.
[07:55] Sofia Tran: Any customers in media you can reference?
[07:58] Maya Chen: We have a couple of podcast search customers — we'll share anonymized references and the case study.
[08:08] [pause / background noise]
[08:15] Priya Nair: One more technical — KV cache and prefix caching — can you explain that in plain terms?
[08:20] Tom Reyes: Sure — prefix/KV cache stores recent transformer key/value states for common prefixes so repeating tokens don't re-compute full attention, which speeds up autoregressive generation. For embeddings/rerank workloads it's less relevant than chat latency but prefix caching is great for conversational rerank scenarios.
[08:40] Diego Alvarez: Hmm I think I saw a note earlier about "KV cash" in the docs — again minor typo but worth fixing.
[08:45] Tom Reyes: Noted, thanks.
[08:48] Priya Nair: For the POC, what's realistic in terms of time to get something running? We want results within two weeks.
[08:54] Maya Chen: Two weeks is typical: day 0-2 share artifacts and data, day 3-7 run bulk embedding jobs and candidate retrieval tuning, day 8-12 rerank evaluation and iterate, day 13-14 present results.
[09:10] Sofia Tran: Ok good. We'll aim to provide sample data by Friday.
[09:13] Priya Nair: Are there any compliance questionnaires we need to fill?
[09:16] Maya Chen: We have a security questionnaire and can do an NDA if needed; we'll attach standard SOC2 artifacts and the security questionnaire in the pack.
[09:25] Diego Alvarez: For the rerank model, how do you handle model updates? We don't want quality regressions mid-POC.
[09:30] Tom Reyes: We support pinning model versions for a rollout, and Redwood Console has rollouts/canary controls so you can pin to rw-rerank-v1 for the POC. If we recommend an update, we do A/B testing.
[09:42] Priya Nair: Any limitations on candidate set size?
[09:45] Tom Reyes: Practically you want to rerank top 50-200; above that cost and latency ramp quickly. We can help profile the sweet spot with your data.
[09:56] Maya Chen: Quick note — we'll include a small sample script to convert your transcript chunks into the candidate format and a FAISS example for retrieval if you want to keep your own vector store.
[10:06] Diego Alvarez: About keeping our own vector store — we currently use Pinecone; is that supported?
[10:10] Tom Reyes: Yep, we integrate with Pinecone and FAISS; you can use your Pinecone for retrieval and call Redwood rerank, or use Redwood embeddings and a client-side vector store. Both patterns are common.
[10:22] Sofia Tran: Ok, any red flags or blockers we should be aware of?
[10:25] Priya Nair: Data residency and KMS are the two main ones for us.
[10:29] Maya Chen: We'll provide region controls and KMS options; Private deployment is an option for fully on-prem.
[10:35] Tom Reyes: Wrapping up the technical part — next I'll demo a quick end-to-end scoring pipeline with a small sample.
[11:20] Tom Reyes: Here's a sample result: query "best episode about urban gardening" — top candidates ranked and reranked by rw-rerank-v1, you can see the score delta compared to plain embedding cosine.
[12:25] Priya Nair: Nice, looks like rerank improves ordering for mid-tail queries.
[12:30] Maya Chen: Great. To recap, agreed actions: we'll send pricing & security pack, Tom will share the benchmark sheet and sample scripts, and SoundWave will provide 1k queries + gold labels.
[12:45] Sofia Tran: Sounds good. If we see promising results we may spin up a Dedicated trial for a subset of traffic.
[12:54] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll include Dedicated sizing notes in the pack.
[13:03] Maya Chen: Hosted has a best-effort SLA; Dedicated offers contractual SLAs. We'll include details.
[13:10] Diego Alvarez: Ok, sending sample data by Friday.
[13:13] Priya Nair: Thanks, Maya and Tom.
[13:17] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and sheet.
[13:22] [End of meeting]
